items.title: HackMe 0.1.0-rc14 is live — pool fuzz customer-first priority
items.summary: E2E customer order flow on Aug 11: rc14 reduced claim latency from seconds to milliseconds and improved pool throughput for real customer orders. Customer order completed 256/256 in ~26 minutes; hybrid dig is ON on customer campaigns; escrow 20/80 unchanged.
items.impact: Evidence for correct pool scheduling + fuzz integration: claim path priority, customer-first ordering, and hybrid dig/fuzz runs that produce findings on customer campaigns. Not a claim of trustless L1 / exchange readiness / CEX readiness.

items.title: Overnight pool win — 2000/2000 cjson + jsmn catch-up settled
items.summary: Customer bootstrap path held through the night: overnight cjson Audit finished 2000/2000 with escrow closed clean; jsmn recovered from a frozen ~1421 settle tip to full catch-up (~22.6k runs paid). Distributed workerfuzz + PoH auto-switch kept the marketplace honest without fake CVE theater.
items.impact: Proof that pool-distributed B2B audits can run unattended overnight — runs complete, escrow settles, CI crash-first gate stays the deliverable. Operators get a cleaner morning marketplace (zombie yyjson cancelled; live work is real progress).

items.title: B2B audits that CI can trust — crash-first reports · honest Scan/Audit/Deep
items.summary: Customer path is productized: register → wizard (Scan · Audit · Deep) → status → HTML report + CI gate. Crash-first triage means detector noise never fails the gate. Escrow 20/80 stays transparent; PoH miners auto-switch to orders while workerfuzz fleets dig pool fuzz. Example: HackMe Bootstrap Audit · cjson — runs progressing, gate crash-first, clean / no critical crash-class.
items.impact: Protocol and security teams get a deliverable they can wire into pipelines — PASS/FAIL on crash-class findings only, plus an honest assurance note (not proven secure). No fake CVE theater: CLEAN means no crash/hang/ASan/memory at the budgeted runs.
